facts.text: After the resolution of Complete Independence was passed in the Lahore session, Mahatma Gandhi decided to launch the Civil Disobedience Movement.
facts.quote: After the resolution of Complete Independence was passed in the Lahore session, Mahatma Gandhi decided to launch the Civil Disobedience Movement.

facts.text: An important demand of Gandhiji was to cancel the salt tax and the British Government's monopoly over the manufacture of salt; when his demands were rejected he decided to break the salt act.
facts.quote: One of the important demand was to cancel the salt tax and monopoly of British Government for manufacture of salt. But because the demands of Gandhiji were rejected by the Government he decided to launch Satyagraha all over India by breaking the salt act.

facts.text: Salt is an important ingredient in the food of common people, so taxing it was unjust; the Salt Satyagraha was symbolic, aiming to break the oppressive and unjust British laws through peace and Satyagraha.
facts.quote: Salt is an important ingredient in the food of common people. Hence it was unjust to impose tax on an essential commodity like salt. ... Salt Satyagraha was symbolic. The extensive objective behind it was to break the oppressive and unjust laws of the British Government through peace and Satyagraha.

facts.text: Gandhiji chose Dandi, a seashore in Gujarat, to begin the Salt Satyagraha.
facts.quote: Gandhiji chose Dandi, a seashore, in Gujarat to begin the Salt Satyagraha.

facts.text: On 12 March 1930 Gandhiji set out from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers for launching the Salt Satyagraha.
facts.quote: On 12 March 1930 Gandhiji set out from Sabarmati Ashram with 78 followers for launching the Salt Satyagraha.

facts.text: A distance of approximately 385 km was covered on foot, and Gandhiji delivered speeches in the villages on the way.
facts.quote: A distance of approximately 385 km was covered on foot and Gandhiji delivered speeches in the villages on the way.

facts.text: On 5 April 1930 Gandhiji reached Dandi.
facts.quote: On 5 April 1930, Gandhiji reached Dandi.

facts.text: On 6 April 1930 Gandhiji broke the salt act by picking up salt on the sea shore of Dandi, and the Civil Disobedience Movement started all over the country.
facts.quote: On 6 April Gandhiji broke the salt act by picking up the salt laying on the sea shore of Dandi and the Civil Disobedience Movement started all over the country.

facts.text: Khan Abdul Gafar Khan of the North West Frontier, the most loyal follower of Mahatma Gandhi, was known as 'Frontier Gandhi' and founded 'Khuda-i-Khidmatgar'.
facts.quote: In the North West Frontier, Khan Abdul Gafar Khan was the most loyal follower of Mahatma Gandhi. He was also known as 'Frontier Gandhi'. He had founded the organisation called 'Khuda-i-Khidmatgar'.

facts.text: On 23 April 1930 Khan Abdul Gafar Khan started satyagraha at Peshawar; the town was in the hands of the satyagrahis nearly for a week.
facts.quote: On 23 April 1930, he started satyagraha at Peshawar. The town was in the hands of the satyagrahis nearly for a week.

facts.text: The Garhwal regiment was ordered to fire on the satyagrahis, but Chandrasing Thakur, an officer of the Garhwal Regiment, refused; he was court martialled and severely punished.
facts.quote: The British Government gave orders to the Garhwal regiment to carry out open firing on the Satyagrahis, but Chandrasing Thakur, an officer of Garhwal Regiment, refused to open fire. He was court martialled and was given a severe punishment.

facts.text: On 4 May 1930 Gandhiji was arrested, and there was protest all over the country.
facts.quote: On 4 May 1930 Gandhiji was arrested. ... There was protest all over the country due to the arrest of Mahatma Gandhi.

facts.text: Mill workers were on the forefront of the Solapur satyagraha; on 6 May 1930 a hartal was observed in Solapur, and the District Collector ordered firing on a huge procession.
facts.quote: The mill workers were on the forefront in the Solapur satyagraha. On 6 May 1930, hartal was observed in Solapur. A huge procession was organised in Solapur. The District Collector gave orders of firing on the procession.

facts.text: Many volunteers along with Shankar Shivdare died in the Solapur firing; people attacked police stations and other buildings, and the Government declared Martial Law.
facts.quote: Many volunteers along with Shankar Shivdare died in the firing. As a result, people started attacking police stations, railway station, courts, municipal buildings etc. The Government declared Martial Law and the agitation was supressed.

facts.text: Solapur leaders Mallappa Dhanshetti, Shrikrishna Sarda, Qurban Hussain and Jagannath Shinde were hanged to death.
facts.quote: Those who took lead in this movement, such as Mallappa Dhanshetti, Shrikrishna Sarda, Qurban Hussain and Jagannath Shinde were hanged to death.

facts.text: The satyagraha at Dharasana in Gujarat was led by Sarojini Naidu; the satyagrahis silently tolerated lathi blows, and when some were taken for medical aid another batch replaced them.
facts.quote: The satyagraha at Dharasana in Gujarat was led by Sarojini Naidu. The police lathi charged on the satyagrahis who came forward to break the Salt Act. The satyagrahis silently tolerated the blows of the lathi. When they were taken away for medical aid, another batch of satyagrahis came forward to replace them.

facts.text: In Maharashtra, salt satyagraha took place at Wadala, Malvan and Shiroda.
facts.quote: In Maharashtra, salt satyagraha took place at Wadala, Malvan and Shiroda.

facts.text: Where there were no salt-pans, forest laws were broken: jungle satyagrahas took place at Bilashi, Sangamner, Kalavan, Chirner and Pusad in Maharashtra, with tribal people taking part in large numbers.
facts.quote: Where there were no salt-pans, the forest laws were broken. There were jungle satyagrahas at Bilashi, Sangamner, Kalavan, Chirner and Pusad in Maharashtra. The tribal people also took part in the satyagraha in large numbers.

facts.text: Babu Genu Said, a mill worker from Mumbai, lay down on the road to stop a truck carrying foreign goods and was crushed under it; his sacrifice inspired the national movement.
facts.quote: Babu Genu Said, a mill worker, from Mumbai was in the forefront in this movement. A truck carrying foreign goods, safeguarded by the police, came in front of Babu Genu. To stop the truck he lied down on the road. ... Finally he was crushed under the truck. Babu Genu gained martyrdom.

facts.text: Do you know: earlier movements were limited only to urban areas, but the Civil Disobedience Movement became nationwide, with people from rural areas taking part.
facts.quote: All the movements, till now, were limited only to urban areas. But this movement became a nationwide movement. People from rural areas registered their participation.

facts.text: Do you know: women took part in large numbers; Kasturba Gandhi, Kamladevi Chattopadhyay, Avantikabai Gokhale, Lilavati Munshi and Hansaben Mehta led the satyagraha.
facts.quote: Women also took part in large numbers. Kasturba Gandhi, Kamladevi Chattopadhyay, Avantikabai Gokhale, Lilavati Munshi, Hansaben Mehta led the satyagraha.

facts.text: Do you know: the movement was based on complete non violence; people protested unarmed and became fearless.
facts.quote: This movement was based on complete non violence. ... the people protested unarmed. Due to this the Indian people became fearless.

facts.text: British Prime Minister Ramsay Mac Donald organised a conference at London known as the 'Round Table Conference'; three were held between 1930 and 1932.
facts.quote: For this purpose he organised a conference at London. This conference is known as 'Round Table Conference'. In the period between 1930 to 1932, three round table conferences were organised.

facts.text: Ramsay MacDonald chaired the First Round Table Conference; participants included Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru and Barrister Jinnah, and topics included Responsible Government at central level and a federal State.
facts.quote: Ramsay MacDonald was the chairman of the Round Table Conference. ... These included Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, Barrister Jinnah etc. In the conference there were discussions on various topics such as Responsible Government at central level, establishment of federal State in India etc.

facts.text: The Indian National Congress did not participate in the First Round Table Conference, so its deliberations were meaningless.
facts.quote: However, the Indian National Congress did not participate in it. ... Without its participation, the deliberations in the Round Table Conference were indeed meaningless.

facts.text: On the Prime Minister's appeal the Viceroy released Gandhi; the Gandhi-Irwin Pact assured Responsible Government in the proposed constitution, and Congress withdrew the movement and agreed to attend the Round Table Conference.
facts.quote: the Viceroy released Mahatma Gandhi and other leaders from prison. ... A pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Irwin which is known as the 'Gandhi-Irwin Pact'. ... Consequently Indian National Congress withdrew the Civil Disobedience Movement and agreed to attend the Round Table Conference.

facts.text: In 1931 the second round table conference was organised; Mahatma Gandhi attended as the representative of the Indian National Congress, failed to bring unanimity on the issue of minorities and returned disappointed.
facts.quote: In 1931, the second round table conference was organised. Mahatma Gandhi attended this conference as a representative of the Indian National Congress. ... The Government put forth the issue of minorities ... Finally Gandhiji became disappointed and returned back to India.

facts.text: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar represented the Dalits and demanded separate electorates; after the Second Round Table Conference Ramsay MacDonald declared the 'Communal Awards', giving Dalits separate electorates.
facts.quote: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar represented the Dalits in the Round Table Conference. He demanded seperate electorates for the Dalits. After the Second Round Table Conference the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald declared 'Communal Awards'. According to it, Dalits were given seperate electorates.

facts.text: Gandhiji went on fast unto death at Yerwada jail protesting against separate electorates on the basis of caste.
facts.quote: Gandhiji went on fast unto death at Yerwada jail protesting against the granting of seperate electorate on the basis of caste.

facts.text: In 1932 Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar signed the Poona Pact: separate electorates for the Dalits were cancelled and reserved seats were provided.
facts.quote: In 1932 Mahatma Gandhi and Dr.Babasaheb Ambedkar signed the famous Poona Pact. According to this pact seperate electorates for the Dalits was cancelled and a provision for reserved seats was made.

facts.text: In November 1932 the Third Round Table Conference was organised in England; the Congress boycotted it and it proved futile.
facts.quote: In November 1932 the Third Round Table Conference was organised in England. The Indian National Congress boycotted the conference. Thus this conference proved to be futile.

facts.text: Back from the Second Round Table Conference with a dejected mind, Gandhiji restarted the Civil Disobedience Movement and was immediately arrested.
facts.quote: Gandhiji returned to India from the Second Round Table Conference with a dejected mind. He decided to restart the Civil Disobedience Movement. Gandhiji was immediately arrested.

facts.text: The Government used oppressive methods: the Congress and its associated institutions were declared illegal and restrictions were levied on national newspapers and literature.
facts.quote: The Indian National Congress and its associated institutions were declared illegal. Restrictions were levied on national newspaper and literature.

facts.text: In April 1934 Gandhiji withdrew the movement and the historic phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement came to an end.
facts.quote: Finally in April 1934 Gandhiji withdrew the movement and the historic phase of Civil Disobedience Movement came to an end.
